contested_claims.claim: How much of the longer passage on Jesus (Antiquities XVIII.3.3) Josephus wrote
contested_claims.sides: Ancient: our copies read 'He was [the] Christ' (josephus_works-antiquities-wars-life_whiston1859 l.81411) and Eusebius quotes it so (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.9232); Origen says Josephus 'did not accept Jesus as Christ' (anf09_gospel-of-peter-diatessaron-origen-commentaries l.30628); Jerome's version reads 'was believed to be Christ' (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.39729). Modern, in McGiffert's 1890 note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.9184-9226): wholly genuine (few; McGiffert: untenable); wholly added (Hase, Keim, Schürer, McGiffert); partly genuine (Gieseler, Weizsäcker, Renan, Edersheim, Schaff); a hostile passage rewritten (Ewald). Whiston defends the whole as genuine (josephus_works-antiquities-wars-life_whiston1859 l.138236-138252).

claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.4.3, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39968-39984)

claims.claim: 'Around 150': Justin, writing while Marcion was 'even at this day alive, and teaching', counts 'one hundred and fifty years' from Christ's birth in the same Apology; Tertullian places Marcion 'in the reign of Antoninus'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 26 and 46, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14943-14944, 15680-15681); Tertullian, Prescription 30 and Against Marcion I.19, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.21334, 23721-23727)

claims.claim: Marcion came from Pontus, on the Black Sea (the Euxine)
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 26 and 58 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14943, 16131); Irenaeus I.27.2 (l.33572); Tertullian, Against Marcion I.1-2, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.22516, 22609)

claims.claim: The churches Marcion founded took his name: 'It too, of course, has its churches ... with Marcion forsooth as their founder'; the tradition is Marcion / Marcionism
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against Marcion IV.5, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.29323-29330); world census, marcion-marcionism

claims.claim: Polycarp, appointed bishop of Smyrna and 'a very old man', 'coming to Rome in the time of Anicetus caused many to turn away from the aforesaid heretics', Valentinus and Marcion
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.3.4, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39857-39875)

claims.claim: Marcion met Polycarp 'on one occasion' and asked 'Dost thou know me?'; Polycarp answered 'I do know thee, the first-born of Satan'; Irenaeus adds 'Such was the horror ... against holding even verbal communication with any corrupters of the truth'. Told in modern English as 'Do you recognize us?' and 'I recognize, I recognize the first-born of Satan', after the held originals
claims.witness: Irenaeus III.3.4, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39882-39886); Moscow epilogue of the Martyrdom of Polycarp, ed. Gebhardt (acta-martyrum-selecta_gebhardt1902 l.1054-1056); Hadrian I, MGH Epistolae 5 (hadrian-i_epistolae-karolini-aevi-3-mgh-epistolae-5-lat_1899 l.17230-17231); Eusebius IV.14, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22977-22984). One witness to the event, Irenaeus, a partisan.

claims.claim: 'Asking to be owned as a brother' is the sense of the verb (recognize, acknowledge) and of Irenaeus's following sentence on refusing communication with corrupters of the truth
claims.witness: Irenaeus III.3.4 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39884-39886); the held originals as above; renderings comparison E24

claims.claim: None of Marcion's own books survives; nearly all that is known of him comes from opponents. Justin says the devils put him forward; Irenaeus says he spoke 'with the mouth of the devil'
claims.witness: Statement about the record (no held file contains a work of his); Justin, First Apology 58 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.16130-16131); Irenaeus I.27.3 (l.33599-33600)

claims.claim: Justin, while Marcion lived, says he taught his disciples 'to believe in some other god greater than the Creator'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 26, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14943-14945)

claims.claim: For Marcion the God of the law and the prophets was not the Father of Jesus; Jesus came from 'that father who is above the God that made the world'; 'The heretic of Pontus introduces two Gods'
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.27.1-2, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.33567-33568, 33572-33582); Tertullian, Against Marcion I.2, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.22609-22612). Two independent witnesses to the teaching, with Justin a third

claims.claim: 'Marcion's special and principal work is the separation of the law and the gospel'; the Antitheses were compiled for 'such a severance of the law from the gospel as should divide the Deity into two'
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against Marcion I.19 and IV.1, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.23735-23736, 28903-28910)

claims.claim: To fit the teaching he cut down Luke's Gospel, removing what shows the Maker as Christ's Father, and the letters of Paul
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.27.2 and III.11.7 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.33582-33594, 41032-41034); Tertullian, Against Marcion IV.2 and V.1, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.29097-29103, 36484-36489)

claims.claim: Marcion at first believed in the doctrine of the church at Rome and gave it money, which the church rejected along with him; he was expelled
claims.witness: Tertullian, Prescription 30 and Against Marcion IV.4, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.21335-21344, 29237-29243). One witness; not in Justin, First Apology 26 and 58, nor Irenaeus I.27, III.3.4 or III.4.3, where it is Cerdo who is put out (anf01 l.39976-39983)

claims.claim: In his lifetime he had caused 'many of every nation' to follow; 'this man many have believed'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 26 and 58, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14945-14946, 16135)

claims.claim: Tertullian mocks yet grants that the Marcionites had churches of their own: 'Even wasps make combs; so also these Marcionites make churches'
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against Marcion IV.5, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.29323-29330)

claims.claim: Irenaeus argued 'It is not possible that the Gospels can be either more or fewer in number than they are', four, and named Marcion among those who make them fewer
claims.witness: Irenaeus III.11.8-9, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.41044-41058, 41142-41149); III.11.7 (l.41032-41034)

claims.claim: Tertullian wrote five books against Marcion and in the fourth refuted him from Marcion's own Gospel
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against Marcion I-V, tr. Holmes; IV.1 and IV.4 (anf03_tertullian l.28913-28917, 29246-29249)

claims.claim: Epiphanius says the sect is found 'even now' in Rome and Italy, Egypt and Palestine, Arabia and Syria, Cyprus and the Thebaid, and in Persia
claims.witness: Epiphanius, Panarion 42.1.2, Greek, ed. Holl (epiphanius_panarion-haer-34-64-gcs-bd2-grc_holl1922 l.7464, 7471-7474; l.7464 damaged in the OCR)

claims.claim: Theodoret of Cyrrhus, a bishop in Syria, wrote that he 'led eight villages of Marcionists with their neighbourhood into the way of truth'
claims.witness: Theodoret, Letter 81 to the consul Nomus, tr. Jackson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.31511-31512). One witness, about his own work

claims.claim: 'Two centuries after Marcion' (Epiphanius) and 'a century later' (Theodoret)
claims.witness: World census dates: Epiphanius of Salamis c. 310-403; Theodoret of Cyrrhus 393-c. 458; not stated in their texts

claims.claim: Card: Theodoret also wrote 'more than a thousand souls did I rescue from the plague of Marcion'
claims.witness: Theodoret, Letter 113 to Leo, tr. Jackson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.33162-33163)

claims.claim: Card: Ephrem wrote discourses against Marcion's teaching on the Stranger above the Maker
claims.witness: Ephrem, Prose Refutations, tr. Mitchell (ephraim_prose-refutations_mitchell1912-1921 l.581-584, 1538, 1745, 1833-1834)

claims.claim: Card: shipmaster of Pontus; the two hundred sesterces; the late offer to repent and death before reconciliation
claims.witness: Tertullian alone, Prescription 30, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.21331-21332, 21339-21348)

claims.claim: Card: Cerdo was his predecessor, whose doctrine Marcion developed
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.27.1-2 and III.4.3 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.33564-33573, 39970). One witness

claims.claim: Card: Epiphanius's version: at Rome the elders refused to receive him
claims.witness: Epiphanius, Panarion 42.1-2, ed. Holl (epiphanius_panarion-haer-34-64-gcs-bd2-grc_holl1922 l.7490-7491, 7525-7530)

contested_claims.claim: Marcion was a bishop's son put out of the church for violating a virgin
contested_claims.sides: For: pseudo-Tertullian, Against All Heresies 6, tr. Thelwall (anf03_tertullian l.55756-55764); Epiphanius, Panarion 42.1.3-6 (epiphanius_panarion-haer-34-64-gcs-bd2-grc_holl1922 l.7476-7488). Against: Karl Holl, from Tertullian's silence and his word for Marcion's continence (l.7503-7505; anf03_tertullian l.21360).
Irenaeus: he flourished under Anicetus (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39983-39984). Tertullian: at Rome under Bishop Eleutherus (anf03_tertullian l.21335-21337).

Epiphanius alone names Sinope (epiphanius_panarion-haer-34-64-gcs-bd2-grc_holl1922 l.7476-7477); Holl: the one other writer to name it, Filastrius, depends on Epiphanius (l.7497-7498). Justin and Irenaeus say only Pontus.

contested_claims.claim: The wording of Marcion's question and Polycarp's reply
contested_claims.sides: Printed English (Roberts and Rambaut): 'Dost thou know me?' and 'I do know thee' (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39883-39884). First rendering: 'Do you know me?' and 'I do know you'. Second rendering: 'Do you recognize us?' and 'I do recognize you'. Held originals: 'us', a doubled verb, no 'you' (Gebhardt l.1054-1056; MGH Ep. 5 l.17230-17231); most manuscripts of Eusebius a question, three a command (npnf201 l.22977-22981). Final: 'Do you recognize us?', 'I recognize, I recognize the first-born of Satan.'

absent_details.note: No held file contains a work of his. Tertullian had the Antitheses and Marcion's Gospel before him (anf03_tertullian l.29246-29249); both are lost.
The record read stops with Theodoret's letters (about 448); no held source read tells how the churches ended, and the brief does not say.

claims.claim: Around 150: 'Christ was born one hundred and fifty years ago under Cyrenius'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 46, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.15679-15681)

claims.claim: A Christian could be punished for the name alone: 'from a name neither praise nor punishment could reasonably spring, unless something excellent or base in action be proved'; Ptolemaeus asked 'this only: whether he were a Christian' and punished
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 4, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14037-14060); Second Apology 2 as quoted by Eusebius, Church History IV.17, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24156-24188)

claims.claim: Justin, son of Priscus, of Flavia Neapolis in Palestine, petitions Antoninus Pius 'in behalf of those of all nations who are unjustly hated and wantonly abused, myself being one of them'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 1, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.13960-13969); also Eusebius IV.12, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22648-22652)

claims.claim: Justin lived in Rome: 'I am now living in Rome for the second time'
claims.witness: Martyrdom of Justin 2, tr. M. Dods (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29308-29311)

claims.claim: He was one of the second-century Greek apologists, who wrote in Greek to defend the faith
claims.witness: World census, greek-apologists-second-century, 'The Second-Century Greek Apologists' (cic-website/data/world-census.json); Justin's Greek Apologies, ed. Rauschen (justin-martyr_first-apology-grc_rauschen1911; justin-martyr_second-apology-grc_rauschen1911)

claims.claim: He went as a philosopher from a Stoic to a Peripatetic, a Pythagorean and the Platonists
claims.witness: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 2, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.17421-17450)

claims.claim: An old man he met in a field not far from the sea sent him to the prophets
claims.witness: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 3 and 7, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.17467-17472, 17819-17842)

claims.claim: He still called himself a philosopher: 'Thus, and for this reason, I am a philosopher'
claims.witness: Justin, Dialogue with Trypho 8, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.17851-17857)

claims.claim: Christ is the Word 'of whom every race of men were partakers'; 'those who lived reasonably are Christians, even though they have been thought atheists'; Socrates named among the Greeks
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 46, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.15684-15693); Greek, ed. Rauschen (justin-martyr_first-apology-grc_rauschen1911 l.1230-1233)

claims.claim: Both readings of the Greek μετὰ λόγου are kept: A 'those who lived with reason are Christians, even if they were thought to be atheists'; B 'those who lived by the Word are Christians, even though people thought them atheists'. Verdict: changes meaning; final = A
claims.witness: Second-rendering comparison, E20 (Build/Ministry/Operations/Audits/2026-11-16_era1-standard-v1/renderings/comparison.md); the translators' note, 'with reason,' or 'the Word' (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.15686-15688)

claims.claim: He asked that Christians be judged by their life and doctrine; 'By the mere application of a name, nothing is decided, either good or evil, apart from the actions implied in the name'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 3-4, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14003-14016, 14037-14039)

claims.claim: Eusebius follows the petition with an edict he gives as the emperor's: 'the same emperor having learned also from other brethren in Asia of the injuries of all kinds which they were suffering ... thought it proper to address the following ordinance to the Common Assembly of Asia'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.13, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22652-22667)

claims.claim: The edict's ruling: 'if any one has a matter to bring against any person of this class, merely as such a person, let the accused be acquitted of the charge'
claims.witness: Epistle of Antoninus to the Common Assembly of Asia, printed after the First Apology, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.16615-16620); Eusebius's form, IV.13.7, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22803-22806)

claims.claim: The edict is not genuine: ANF heading '[Regarded as spurious.]'; McGiffert: 'undoubtedly spurious ... probably a forgery of the second century'; Eusebius gives it as Antoninus Pius's though its inscription names Marcus Aurelius
claims.witness: ANF (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.16583-16585); McGiffert's notes (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22675-22686, 22689-22700)

claims.claim: Justin expected to be plotted against: 'I too, therefore, expect to be plotted against and fixed to the stake, by some of those I have named, or perhaps by Crescens, that lover of bravado and boasting'
claims.witness: Justin, Second Apology 3, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.16849-16852); Greek, ed. Rauschen (justin-martyr_second-apology-grc_rauschen1911 l.273-275)

claims.claim: Crescens was a Cynic philosopher: 'a philosopher who emulated the life and manners of the Cynics'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.16, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23795-23797); also the ANF editor's note, 'Crescens, a cynic' (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29209-29211)

claims.claim: Tatian says Crescens 'endeavoured to inflict on Justin, and indeed on me, the punishment of death'
claims.witness: Tatian, Address to the Greeks 19, tr. J. E. Ryland (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.6550-6556)

claims.claim: Eusebius says Justin died 'in consequence of the machinations of Crescens'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.16, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23781-23782, 23875-23877, 24077-24078)

claims.claim: The surviving trial account never names Crescens
claims.witness: Martyrdom of Justin, whole text, tr. M. Dods (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29253-29408), searched; McGiffert: 'In the Acta Crescens is not mentioned' (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23787-23790)

claims.claim: Rusticus: 'Are you not, then, a Christian?' Justin: 'Yes, I am a Christian.' Our modern English: 'So then, you are a Christian?' (second reading the same); the Greek has no negative
claims.witness: Martyrdom of Justin 2, tr. M. Dods (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29312-29314); Greek Acts, ed. Gebhardt (acta-martyrum-selecta_gebhardt1902 l.1353-1354, OCR 'Aowrov' for λοιπὸν)

claims.claim: Six others were tried with him: Chariton, Charito, Euelpistus, Hierax, Paeon, Liberianus
claims.witness: Martyrdom of Justin 3, tr. M. Dods (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29323-29353)

claims.claim: They refused to sacrifice to the gods and were beheaded
claims.witness: Martyrdom of Justin 4-5, tr. M. Dods (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29375-29387, 29396-29405)

claims.claim: The trial account: 'nothing is known as to the date or authorship', 'generally reckoned among the most trustworthy of the Martyria'; the hemlock story 'an absurd addition'; McGiffert: 'probably the third century', 'a comparatively truthful account'
claims.witness: Dods's introductory notice (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29216-29220); McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23767-23771)

claims.claim: Marcion was 'teaching his disciples to believe in some other god greater than the Creator'
claims.witness: Justin, First Apology 26, tr. Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.14943-14945)

claims.claim: Irenaeus quotes Justin's book against Marcion with approval: 'Justin does well say: I would not have believed the Lord Himself, if He had announced any other than He who is our framer, maker, and nourisher'
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies IV.6.2, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.44907-44917); Eusebius, Church History IV.18.9, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24340-24346)

claims.claim: 'A generation later': Irenaeus wrote after Justin's death
claims.witness: World census dates for Irenaeus of Lyon (cic-website/data/world-census.json); Irenaeus already calls Justin's martyrdom past, Against Heresies I.28.1 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.33663-33666)

claims.claim: Tatian was 'a hearer of Justin's' and left the church after his martyrdom
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies I.28.1, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.33663-33666)

claims.claim: Tatian calls him 'the most admirable Justin' and bids 'farewell to the arrogance of Romans and the idle talk of Athenians, and all their ill-connected opinions'
claims.witness: Tatian, Address to the Greeks 18 and 35, tr. J. E. Ryland (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.6526, 7258-7260)

claims.claim: The book against Marcion is lost: 'The work is lost, and we have only the single brief fragment preserved by Irenaeus'
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22457-22460)

claims.claim: Eusebius: the ancients thought his discourses 'so worthy of study' that Irenaeus quotes them
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.18.9, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24340-24343)

claims.claim: Eusebius knew the Dialogue, 'held in the city of Ephesus with Trypho, a most distinguished man among the Hebrews of that day', and quotes it
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.18.6-8, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24300-24326)

claims.claim: The Dialogue is 'the first elaborate exposition of the reasons for regarding Christ as the Messiah of the Old Testament'
claims.witness: Dods and Reith's introductory note (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.13881-13884)

claims.claim: Eusebius calls him 'a genuine lover of the true philosophy'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.8, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.21864-21865)

claims.claim: His martyr's death is 'the universal tradition of antiquity, which is crystallized in his name'; Irenaeus is the first to mention it
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23764-23767)

claims.claim: The two Apologies 'were originally one', the second a supplement
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24218-24222, 24234-24241)

claims.claim: Date of the Apology: Eusebius's Chronicle gives 141; 'most critics are now agreed in putting it ten or more years later', before 161; 'as early as 152'
claims.witness: McGiffert's notes (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24224-24227, 24143-24144)

claims.claim: Date of death: two traditions, under Antoninus Pius or Marcus Aurelius; Rusticus 'became prefect of Rome in 163'; the Chronicon Paschale gives 165
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23774-23780); Dods and Reith's introductory note (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.13868-13873)

claims.claim: Eusebius's quotation of Tatian differs from Tatian's text ('upon Justin' for 'on Justin, and indeed on me'); Dembowski, Zahn and Harnack accuse Eusebius of deception; McGiffert finds the grounds 'very slender', the Tatian manuscripts varying at this point
claims.witness: Tatian, Address 19 (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.6552-6556); Eusebius IV.16.9 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.24073-24078); McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23880-23910, 23970-23996)

contested_claims.sides: Eusebius, Church History IV.16, tr. McGiffert: death 'in consequence of the machinations of Crescens' (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23875-23877, 24077-24078). Against: Tatian's own text shows a plot against Justin and Tatian both, not its success (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.6552-6556); the Martyrdom never names Crescens (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29253-29408); McGiffert: Eusebius's report 'seems to rest solely upon the testimony of Tatian', and Crescens is known 'only from the pen of his bitterest enemies' (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23782-23795).

contested_claims.claim: The year and reign of Justin's death
contested_claims.sides: Two traditions: under Antoninus Pius, or under Marcus Aurelius; McGiffert favors the later, Rusticus prefect from 163 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23774-23780). Dods and Reith: 'nearly certain' under Marcus Aurelius; the Chronicon Paschale gives 165 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.13869-13873). No ancient source used here gives a year.

contested_claims.claim: Eusebius changed Tatian's words on purpose
contested_claims.sides: Dembowski, Zahn and Harnack, as McGiffert reports them: an intentional alteration (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23880-23904). McGiffert: the grounds are 'very slender'; Eusebius's manuscript of Tatian may have read as he quotes, since the three Tatian manuscripts vary at this point (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23970-23996).

contested_claims.claim: The edict to the Common Assembly of Asia is genuine
contested_claims.sides: Eusebius gives it as the emperor's (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22652-22667). ANF prints it '[Regarded as spurious.]' (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.16583-16585); McGiffert: 'undoubtedly spurious', 'almost universally acknowledged to be a forgery'; Wieseler contends for it, 'but no good critic follows him' (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22675-22686).

absent_details.detail: Crescens in the account of the trial
absent_details.note: The Martyrdom of Justin, tr. M. Dods, searched in full (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29253-29408): the name does not occur. Only the ANF editor's note before it names him (l.29209-29211). The Greek Acts, ed. Gebhardt (acta-martyrum-selecta_gebhardt1902), were read at the trial question only (l.1350-1355).

absent_details.detail: An ancient year for Justin's death
absent_details.note: Neither Eusebius nor the Martyrdom gives one. The Chronicon Paschale's 165 is reported by Dods and Reith (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.13872-13873) and is not held; McGiffert reasons from Rusticus's prefecture (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.23779-23780).

claims.claim: Around the year 200 (approximate): Clement 'had charge at that time of the catechetical instruction in Alexandria, so that Origen also, while still a boy, was one of his pupils'; the Stromata 'written during the reign of Severus'; Jerome: 'He flourished moreover during the reigns of Severus and his son Antoninus'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History VI.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33040-33043, 33079-33086); Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men 38, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40278-40279)

claims.claim: Some spoke against Greek philosophy, as if it dragged believers from the faith: 'those who are fond of finding fault'; 'although some have calumniated it ... nor does it drag us away from the faith'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata I.2, tr. William Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27670-27672, 27684-27691)

claims.claim: Clement was a presbyter of Alexandria: 'presbyter of the Alexandrian church'; Alexander: 'Clement, the blessed presbyter'
claims.witness: Jerome, Lives 38, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40249-40250); Eusebius VI.11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33612-33614)

claims.claim: He led the Christian school of Alexandria, where converts were taught: 'the school of the faithful in Alexandria'; 'had charge ... of the catechetical instruction'; 'led the theological school at Alexandria ... and was teacher of the Catechetes'
claims.witness: Eusebius V.10 and VI.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28537-28539, 33040-33043); Jerome, Lives 38, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40250-40252)

claims.claim: His tradition is the Alexandrian Catechetical / Christian-Platonist Tradition, told as the Christian school of Alexandria
claims.witness: World census, alexandria-catechetical (cic-website/data/world-census.json)

claims.claim: He studied under Christian teachers from Greece to Palestine, keeping 'the tradition of the blessed doctrine derived directly from the holy apostles'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata I.1, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27483-27487, 27497-27500); also Eusebius V.11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28719-28758)

claims.claim: 'When I came upon the last (he was the first in power), having tracked him out concealed in Egypt, I found rest.' Our modern English: 'When I had tracked him down, hidden in Egypt, I found rest.' Second reading B: 'Then I met the last of them, who was the first in ability. I tracked him down where he lay hidden in Egypt, and I found rest.' Verdict minor; final = A
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata I.1, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27489-27492); second English witness, McGiffert's Eusebius V.11 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28751-28758); comparison E29 (Build/Ministry/Operations/Audits/2026-11-16_era1-standard-v1/renderings/comparison.md). The Greek is not held

claims.claim: Eusebius judged this teacher was Pantaenus: 'It seems to me that he alludes to the same person also in the first book of his Stromata'
claims.witness: Eusebius V.11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28697-28704)

claims.claim: Pantaenus led the school before Clement; Clement 'having succeeded Pantaenus'
claims.witness: Eusebius V.10 and VI.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28537-28539, 28637-28638, 33040-33041); Jerome, Lives 38 (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40250-40251)

claims.claim: Clement's answer: 'For God is the cause of all good things'; 'Perchance, too, philosophy was given to the Greeks directly and primarily, till the Lord should call the Greeks. For this was a schoolmaster to bring "the Hellenic mind," as the law, the Hebrews, "to Christ."'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata I.5, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27888-27893)

claims.claim: 'Philosophy, therefore, was a preparation, paving the way for him who is perfected in Christ.' Our modern English: 'Philosophy, then, was a preparation,' ... 'paving the way for the one who is made perfect in Christ.' Second reading B: 'So philosophy was a preparation. It cleared the way for the one who is being brought to completion in Christ.' Verdict minor; final = A
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata I.5, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27893-27895); comparison E30 (Build/Ministry/Operations/Audits/2026-11-16_era1-standard-v1/renderings/comparison.md). The Greek is not held

claims.claim: Origen was among his pupils as a boy: 'Origen is known to have been his disciple'
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33043-33080); Jerome, Lives 38, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40277-40278)

claims.claim: Origen later led the same school, 'successor to the presbyter Clement'
claims.witness: Jerome, Lives 54, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40530-40531); Jerome, Letter 84.8, tr. Fremantle (npnf206_jerome-principal-works l.19286-19288)

claims.claim: Jerome: 'Imitating his example Origen wrote ten books of Miscellanies, in which he compares together the opinions held respectively by Christians and by philosophers, and confirms all the dogmas of our religion by quotations from Plato and Aristotle'
claims.witness: Jerome, Letter 70.4, to Magnus, tr. Fremantle (npnf206_jerome-principal-works l.16636-16642)

claims.claim: Asked why he quoted secular literature, Jerome pointed among others to Clement, whose books are 'drawn from the very heart of philosophy'; he calls Clement 'in my judgment the most learned of men'
claims.witness: Jerome, Letter 70.2 and 70.4, tr. Fremantle (npnf206_jerome-principal-works l.16454-16455, 16477-16480, 16626-16636)

claims.claim: The followers of Valentinus 'assign faith to us, the simple, but will have it that knowledge springs up in their own selves (who are saved by nature)'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.3, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.32104-32111); an opponent's report

claims.claim: Clement: knowledge is 'built upon faith'; 'believing, that is the foundation of knowledge'; if one is saved by nature, 'the precepts both of the Old and of the New Testament are, then, superfluous'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata VII.10 and V.1, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.51304-51305, 51352-51353, 40953-40958)

claims.claim: Alexander became bishop of Jerusalem, called to the office with Narcissus
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33504-33507); Jerome, Lives 38 (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40268-40269)

claims.claim: Alexander was Clement's pupil: 'the holy Clement, my master and benefactor'; McGiffert: 'from this passage that we gather that Alexander was a student of Clement's'
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.14, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.34330-34358)

claims.claim: From prison Alexander sent a letter to Antioch by Clement: 'I have sent this letter to you by Clement, the blessed presbyter, a man virtuous and approved ... Being here, in the providence and oversight of the Master, he has strengthened and built up the Church of the Lord'
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33600-33617); Jerome, Lives 38, tr. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40268-40277)

claims.claim: His Stromata keep words from the letters of Valentinus
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.8 and II.20, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.32722, 34289)

claims.claim: McGiffert reads Clement into 'all were driven away by the threat of persecution' and dates his leaving to 202
claims.witness: Eusebius VI.3, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.32670-32674); McGiffert's notes (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28668-28670, 33031-33034)

claims.claim: Of his birth 'we have no certain knowledge'; 'of the place and time of his death we know nothing'; last notice about 212; Richardson: 'Born about 160, died about 217'
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28656-28660, 28674-28675); Richardson's note to Jerome, Lives 38 (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40249)

claims.claim: He was commemorated as a saint in ancient times; Clement VIII dropped his name for suspected heterodoxy
claims.witness: McGiffert's notes (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28676-28678, 17051-17055)

claims.claim: Rufinus: 'we sometimes find in his books passages in which he speaks of the Son as a creature of God', which he puts down to corruption by heretics; Jerome reports it
claims.witness: Rufinus, On the Adulteration of the Works of Origen, tr. Fremantle (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.45352-45358); Jerome's report (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.53613-53620)

contested_claims.claim: Clement's last teacher, found in Egypt, was Pantaenus
contested_claims.sides: Eusebius: 'It seems to me', and Clement names Pantaenus as his teacher in the Hypotyposes (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28697-28704); McGiffert: 'There can be no doubt as to his identity' (l.28751-28752), though the Hypotyposes passage is not preserved (l.28698-28700); the ANF note: 'Most likely Pantænus' (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.27489-27490). Clement himself does not name him in the held Stromata passage.

contested_claims.claim: Clement left Alexandria in 202 in the persecution under Severus
contested_claims.sides: McGiffert reads him into Eusebius VI.3 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28668-28670, 33031-33034). Eusebius's line says only that 'all were driven away' and does not name Clement (l.32670-32674).

absent_details.note: None found in the Stromata, Eusebius's Church History, Jerome's Lives or Jerome's Letters as held (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria; npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine; npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus; npnf206_jerome-principal-works). What the Valentinians held is known here only through Clement, their opponent.

absent_details.detail: An ancient year for Clement's teaching, birth or death
absent_details.note: Eusebius and Jerome give reigns, not years (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.33079-33086; npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.40278-40279). 'Around the year 200' is approximate; 190-202, 212, and 160-217 are McGiffert's and Richardson's reckonings.

Not held. Both renderings were made from Wilson's English, with McGiffert's Eusebius as a second English witness for the first quotation (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28751-28758).

claims.claim: In Diocletian's nineteenth year (303), near the Passion feast, edicts commanded 'that the churches be leveled to the ground and the Scriptures be destroyed by fire'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History VIII.2, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.43480-43489)

claims.claim: Pamphilus, 'my dearest friend', the only presbyter at Caesarea among the martyrs, excelled 'in most sincere devotion to the Divine Scriptures'; tortured with 'continuous and prolonged scrapings' and put in prison; at last punished with his companions
claims.witness: Eusebius, Martyrs of Palestine 7 and 11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.46694-46709, 47072-47078, 47190-47198)

claims.claim: Eusebius wrote of the martyrs of Palestine, and a separate Life of Pamphilus in three books
claims.witness: Eusebius, Martyrs of Palestine 11 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.47080-47083); Church History VII.32.25 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.43040-43044)

claims.claim: Eusebius, 'surnamed Pamphilus, bishop of Caesarea in Palestine'
claims.witness: Socrates I.8, tr. Zenos (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.2970-2972); II.4 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.5801-5803)

claims.claim: 'since I am the first to enter upon the subject, I am attempting to traverse as it were a lonely and untrodden path'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History I.1.3, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.6936-6937)

claims.claim: He gathered matters from earlier writers, 'having plucked like flowers from a meadow the appropriate passages from ancient writers'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History I.1.5 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.6961-6964)

claims.claim: Socrates writes 'the details of what has taken place in the churches since his time to our own day'; Theodoret: 'I shall begin my history from the period at which his terminates'
claims.witness: Socrates I.1, tr. Zenos (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.1864-1867); Theodoret I.1, tr. Jackson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.5219-5222)

claims.claim: Socrates: in the Life of Constantine Eusebius 'has but slightly treated of matters regarding Arius, being more intent on the rhetorical finish of his composition and the praises of the emperor, than on an accurate statement of facts'
claims.witness: Socrates I.1 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.1861-1864)

claims.claim: At Nicaea his own formula was read before the emperor, who approved it and advised 'the insertion of the single word, One-in-essence', which he read 'not in the sense of the affections of bodies'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Letter to his diocese 1 and 4, NPNF 2.4 (npnf204_athanasius-select-works-letters l.19563-19568, 19655-19661); Greek of the word in Socrates I.8, ed. Hussey (socrates_historia-ecclesiastica-tomus1-grc-lat_hussey1853 l.7154-7159, OCR)

claims.claim: 'we did not let it pass without inquiry in what sense they introduced "of the essence of the Father," and "one in essence with the Father"'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Letter to his diocese 5 and 8 (npnf204_athanasius-select-works-letters l.19698-19701, 19866-19867), his own account

claims.claim: Eusebius 'had held aloof for a short time', then 'subscribed it with all the rest' and sent his people the creed with an explanation of homoousios
claims.witness: Socrates I.8 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.2970-2978); Sozomen I.21, 'withheld his assent for a little while' (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.28002-28003); Athanasius, De Decretis 3, 'had denied the day before, but afterwards subscribed' (npnf204_athanasius-select-works-letters l.26780-26781)

claims.claim: Some 'attempted to stigmatize even Eusebius Pamphilus himself as having favored the Arian views'; Socrates defends him
claims.witness: Socrates II.21 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.6914-6920)

claims.claim: Athanasius: 'I have subjoined at the end the letter of Eusebius', who had not denied 'the "one in essence"'
claims.witness: Athanasius, De Decretis 3, NPNF 2.4 (npnf204_athanasius-select-works-letters l.26780-26795), a hostile witness

claims.claim: Socrates used Eusebius's account of the council, 'treating what he has said as an authority', and gave the letter 'as follows in his own words'
claims.witness: Socrates I.8 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.2837-2838, 2866-2868, 2978-2979; the letter to l.3157)

claims.claim: Born not far from 260; died late in 339 or early in 340
claims.witness: McGiffert's prolegomena (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.1121-1122, 2774-2786)

claims.claim: Eustathius of Antioch accused him of perverting the Nicene Creed; he answered that Eustathius held the opinion of Sabellius
claims.witness: Socrates I.23 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.4708-4711)

claims.claim: Escaped prison by an unlawful promise
claims.witness: Potamo at Tyre, in Epiphanius, Panarion 68.8, Petavius's Latin (epiphanius_panarion-haer-48-69-corpus-haereseologicum-t2-pars-posterior-grc-lat_oehler1860 l.44663-44672), a partisan of Athanasius; McGiffert's prolegomena: Potamo 'simply conjectures', and Athanasius says only 'accused of sacrificing' (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.1514-1543)

claims.claim: Constantine told him of the cross of light and 'confirmed his statement by an oath'; Richardson: the account 'has met with doubters from the very beginning, commencing with Eusebius himself'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Life of Constantine I.28, tr. Richardson (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.61196-61211)

claims.claim: He took the name Eusebius Pamphili after Pamphilus's death
claims.witness: McGiffert's note to Church History VII.32.25 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.43009-43012)

claims.claim: He was present when crowds were put to death in a day in the Thebaid
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History VIII.9.4 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.44267-44269)

claims.claim: Acacius, his disciple, succeeded him and wrote a sketch of his life
claims.witness: Socrates II.4 (npnf202_socrates-sozomen-ecclesiastical-histories l.5801-5805)

contested_claims.claim: Escaped prison by an unlawful promise
contested_claims.sides: Potamo of Heraclea, at Tyre in 335, in Epiphanius, Panarion 68.8 (partisan, on the side of Athanasius), for. Against: Arthur McGiffert, who calls it Potamo's conjecture, and notes that Athanasius says only that Eusebius was "accused of sacrificing".

contested_claims.claim: Whether Eusebius kept to the Nicene creed
contested_claims.sides: Eustathius of Antioch accused him of perverting it; Eusebius denied it and charged Eustathius with Sabellianism (Socrates I.23). Socrates II.21 defends him against the charge of favoring Arius; Athanasius, De Decretis 3, uses his letter to show he signed.

absent_details.detail: The Greek of Church History Book I
absent_details.note: Not held; the quotation follows McGiffert's English.

absent_details.detail: The years of his birth and death
absent_details.note: No held ancient source gives them; McGiffert reckons them.

claims.claim: Hermas wrote the Pastor 'very recently in our times in the city of Rome, while his brother bishop Pius sat in the chair of the Church of Rome'; 'it also ought to be read; but it cannot be made public in the Church to the people, nor placed among the prophets ... nor among the apostles'
claims.witness: Muratorian Canon, tr. in ANF 5 (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.60178-60185)

claims.claim: The Muratorian report is the earliest held report on who Hermas was and when he wrote; McGiffert: 'The only direct testimony of antiquity is that of the Muratorian Fragment'
claims.witness: Muratorian Canon (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.60178-60180); McGiffert's note to Eusebius III.3 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14776-14779)

claims.claim: 'Around the year 150': Hyginus became bishop of Rome in the first year of Antoninus Pius, held office four years, and Pius held it fifteen
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.10-11, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22121-22123, 22320-22322, 22370-22371); McGiffert's note citing Lipsius, 139-154 earliest, 141-156 latest (l.22328-22331)

claims.claim: Eusebius ascribes the Shepherd to the Hermas whom Paul greets in Romans 16: the apostle 'has made mention among others of Hermas, to whom the book called The Shepherd ... is ascribed'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History III.3.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14735-14736, 14753-14754, 14848)

claims.claim: Jerome: the Hermas of Romans 16 'is reputed to be the author of the book which is called Pastor and which is also read publicly in some churches of Greece ... but among the Latins it is almost unknown'
claims.witness: Jerome, Lives of Illustrious Men 10, tr. E. C. Richardson (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.39614-39629)

claims.claim: Everything else told of his life comes from inside his own visions; no other held witness gives any fact of his life
claims.witness: The Shepherd, Vision 1 onward, tr. F. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.646 onward); no other held ancient witness found

claims.claim: 'He who had brought me up, sold me to one Rhode in Rome. Many years after this I recognised her, and I began to love her as a sister'; the thought 'I should be a happy man if I could but get a wife as handsome and good as she is'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Vision 1.1, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.648-658); his own visionary account

claims.claim: In a vision 'I see the woman whom I had desired saluting me from the sky'; she: 'I have been taken up here to accuse you of your sins before the Lord'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Vision 1.1, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.681-685); a vision

claims.claim: 'I was overwhelmed with sorrow and fear, and said to myself, "If this sin is assigned to me, how can I be saved"'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Vision 1.2, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.733-734)

claims.claim: Hermas heard 'some teachers maintain that there is no other repentance than that which takes place, when we descended into the water'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Commandment 4.3, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1990-1994)

claims.claim: The angel came 'dressed like a shepherd', 'sent by a most venerable angel to dwell with you the remaining days of your life'; 'the shepherd, even the angel of repentance'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Vision 5, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1695-1700, 1724-1725)

claims.claim: The angel: 'That was sound doctrine'; 'he who has received remission of his sins ought not to sin any more'; 'those who have now believed, and those who are to believe, have not repentance ... For to those who have been called before these days, the Lord has set repentance'; the Lord 'knew the weakness of men' and 'being merciful ... has set repentance for them'; 'he has opportunity to repent but once'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Commandment 4.3, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1994-2020)

claims.claim: The husband must take back a wife who repents: 'he ought to take back the sinner who has repented. But not frequently. For there is but one repentance to the servants of God'
claims.witness: Hermas, The Shepherd, Commandment 4.1, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1924-1934)

claims.claim: Quotation 'For the servants of God there is only one repentance.' Rendering A: 'For the servants of God there is only one repentance.' Rendering B: 'For the servants of God have only one repentance.' Verdict same; FINAL = A
claims.witness: Printed: Commandment 4.1, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1933-1934); Build/Ministry/Operations/Audits/2026-11-16_era1-standard-v1/renderings/comparison.md E18; the Greek is not held

claims.claim: Irenaeus quotes the Shepherd as Scripture: 'Truly, then, the Scripture declared, which says, "First of all believe that there is one God"'; Eusebius: Irenaeus 'not only knows, but also receives, The Shepherd'
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies IV.20.2, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.46864-46868); Eusebius, Church History V.8.7, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.28248-28257)

claims.claim: Tertullian attacks a bishop's edict: 'I remit, to such as have discharged (the requirements of) repentance, the sins both of adultery and of fornication'
claims.witness: Tertullian, On Modesty 1, tr. S. Thelwall (anf04_tertullian4-minucius-felix-commodian-origen1-2 l.7178-7189)

claims.claim: Tertullian: the Shepherd 'is the only one which favours adulterers'; 'habitually judged by every council of Churches (even of your own) among apocryphal and false (writings)'; Latin 'quae sola moechos amat ... ab omni concilio ecclesiarum, etiam uestrarum, inter apocrypha et falsa iudicaretur'; elsewhere 'that apocryphal "Shepherd" of adulterers'
claims.witness: Tertullian, On Modesty 10 and 20, tr. Thelwall (anf04_tertullian4-minucius-felix-commodian-origen1-2 l.8138-8144, 9330-9331); Latin, CSEL 20, ed. Reifferscheid and Wissowa (tertullian_opera-pars1-lat_reifferscheid-wissowa-csel20 l.13578-13581); a hostile witness, and his report of the councils is his alone

claims.claim: Eusebius counts the Shepherd among the rejected writings (ἐν τοῖς νόθοις); yet 'by others it is considered quite indispensable, especially to those who need instruction in the elements of the faith. Hence, as we know, it has been publicly read in churches'
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History III.25.4 and III.3.6, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.18031-18034, 14854-14860)

claims.claim: McGiffert: Clement of Alexandria and Origen 'often quote it as an inspired book, though the latter expressly distinguishes it from the canonical books'
claims.witness: McGiffert's note to Eusebius III.3 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14759-14761); a modern statement, on the card only

claims.claim: McGiffert: the Muratorian testimony 'is accepted by the majority of scholars'; Zahn 'dates it between 97 and 100, and assigns it to an unknown Hermas, a contemporary of the Roman Clement', followed by Salmon; the Clement mention (Vis. II.4.3) makes a contemporary of Clement 'very likely' but not certain
claims.witness: McGiffert's note to Eusebius III.3 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14776-14808); Hermas, Vision 2.4, tr. Crombie (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.1010-1013)

claims.claim: The identification with the Hermas of Romans 16 'appears to be no older than Origen, with whom it is no more than a mere guess'; Richardson's note: 'this view of Jerome taken from Origen through Eusebius is not much accepted'
claims.witness: McGiffert's note (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14793-14795); note in Richardson's Jerome (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.39614-39618)

claims.claim: Coxe's bracketed note on Commandment 4.3: 'Can the following words be genuine? They reflect the very Montanism here so strictly opposed'; the clause 'In ... life' 'occur only in Pal.'
claims.witness: A. Cleveland Coxe's note, ANF 2 (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.2015-2019)

claims.claim: Opening variants: Vatican 'He who had brought me up, sold a certain young woman at Rome'; 'Pal. has the name of the woman, Rada'; 'The name Rhode occurs in Acts xii. 13'
claims.witness: Editor's note to Vision 1.1, ANF 2 (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.649-652)

claims.claim: Tradition: Post-Apostolic Household-Church Christianity
claims.witness: cic-website/data/world-census.json, tradition post-apostolic-house-church, which lists hermas

contested_claims.claim: Who Hermas was and when the Shepherd was written
contested_claims.sides: The Muratorian Canon: the brother of Bishop Pius, writing 'very recently in our times' (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.60178-60180), accepted by the majority of scholars in McGiffert's day (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14780-14782). Eusebius III.3.6 (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.14735-14736, 14753) and Jerome, Lives 10 (npnf203_theodoret-jerome-gennadius-rufinus l.39614-39627): the Hermas greeted in Romans 16, a view McGiffert calls 'a mere guess' of Origen's (l.14793-14795). Zahn, followed by Salmon: an unknown Hermas writing 97-100, in Clement's time (l.14807-14809).

absent_details.detail: Any fact of his life outside his own visions, and what became of him
absent_details.note: No held ancient witness (the Muratorian Canon, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Eusebius, Jerome) tells his life beyond the book or his end. The Rhoda story and his household are the visions' own frame.

absent_details.detail: An ancient witness that the churches took up his one repentance as a rule
absent_details.note: None found in the held files; the brief does not claim it, and the old card's 'shaped the Roman teaching' was dropped for want of a witness.

claims.claim: 'Valentinus came to Rome in the time of Hyginus, flourished under Pius, and remained until Anicetus', that is, through two more bishops
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies III.4.3, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39968-39970). One witness, a partisan

claims.claim: 'Around 140': Hyginus became bishop of Rome in the first year of Antoninus Pius
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History IV.10, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.22120-22126); Irenaeus III.4.3 (anf01 l.39968-39970)

claims.claim: Other rival teachers came to Rome in those years: Cerdo arrived in the time of Hyginus, and Marcion succeeded him
claims.witness: Irenaeus III.4.3 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39970-39984)

claims.claim: Irenaeus wrote against them all
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies I (Valentinians), I.27 (Cerdo and Marcion) (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29844-29873, 33564-33594)

claims.claim: His followers were called Valentinians
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against the Valentinians 4, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.43104-43106, 43124-43125)

claims.claim: Theirs was one of the Gnostic Christianities: Valentinus 'adapted the principles of the heresy called "Gnostic" to the peculiar character of his own school'; the tradition is Valentinian & other Gnostic Christianities
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.11.1 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.31520-31521); world census, valentinian-and-other-gnostic-christianities

claims.claim: They claimed a knowledge higher than faith: 'the followers of Valentinus assign faith to us, the simple, but will have it that knowledge springs up in their own selves'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.3, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.32106-32111); Irenaeus I.6.2 (anf01 l.30754-30757)

claims.claim: Valentinus 'had expected to become a bishop, because he was an able man both in genius and eloquence'; when another obtained it 'by reason of a claim which confessorship had given him, he broke with the church'; ambition and revenge
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against the Valentinians 4, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.43109-43115). Tertullian alone, a hostile witness; not in Irenaeus I.11 or III.4.3 nor in Clement

claims.claim: His own words survive only in a few passages his opponents quote, most of them in Clement, who quotes them in order to answer them; the Refutation also quotes a psalm and tells a vision
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.8, II.20, IV.13, VI.6, tr. Wilson (anf02 l.32722-32736, 34289-34314, 39090-39112, 46642-46652); Refutation VI, tr. MacMahon (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.9787-9802, 10053-10057)

claims.claim: In a letter Valentinus compares the heart to a caravanserai, 'filled with dung; men living filthily in it', 'the abode of many demons'; 'But when the only good Father visits it, it is sanctified, and gleams with light.' 'Roadside inn' is our plain word for caravanserai
claims.witness: Valentinus, letter, in Clement, Stromata II.20, tr. Wilson (anf02_hermas-tatian-athenagoras-theophilus-clement-alexandria l.34289-34302)

claims.claim: Clement had Valentinus's own letters before him: 'Valentinus too, in a letter to certain people, writes in these very words'
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.20 and II.8 (anf02 l.34289-34290, 32722-32723)

claims.claim: Valentinus placed the Maker of this world below a higher, unseen God
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.11.1 and IV preface 3 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.31535-31543, 44340-44342); Clement, Stromata IV.13, quoting Valentinus: the world inferior to the living Aeon, the Creator the 'Painter', 'to the glory of the invisible One' (anf02 l.39100-39110). Two witnesses

claims.claim: His school held that its members were saved by nature, while ordinary believers needed faith
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata II.3, II.20, IV.13 (anf02 l.32106-32109, 34308-34309, 39095-39096); Irenaeus I.6.2 (anf01 l.30754-30763). Two witnesses

claims.claim: Irenaeus sets out a fuller system, which Clement does not confirm: a Dyad, a Tetrad and the Ogdoad of powers in pairs; one of the twelve, 'falling from its original condition, produced the rest of the universe'
claims.witness: Irenaeus I.11.1 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.31522-31531). One witness for the system as Valentinus's; Clement's 'things which proceed from a pair are complements' (anf02 l.39110-39111) is too thin to confirm it

claims.claim: The school carried on under teachers the opponents name, Ptolemy and Heracleon among them
claims.witness: Irenaeus I preface 2 and II.4.1 (anf01 l.29872-29873, 34634); Clement, Stromata IV.9, 'Heracleon, the most distinguished of the school of Valentinians' (anf02 l.38779-38780); Tertullian, Against the Valentinians 4 (anf03_tertullian l.43117-43123, printed 'Heraclean')

claims.claim: Irenaeus had read the disciples' Commentaries and met some of them; he feared some would be carried off 'because their language resembles ours, while their sentiments are very different', and so wrote
claims.witness: Irenaeus I preface 2, tr. Roberts and Rambaut (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29844-29867)

claims.claim: His five books Against Heresies
claims.witness: Irenaeus, Against Heresies I-V (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.29777, 34224, 39621, 44299, 50523)

claims.claim: Earlier writers 'were unable ... to refute the Valentinians satisfactorily, because they were ignorant of these men's system'; 'they who overthrow them, do in fact overthrow every kind of heresy'
claims.witness: Irenaeus IV preface 2 (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.44326-44338)

claims.claim: Card: Clement had read Irenaeus and gave extracts from his writings
claims.witness: Eusebius, Church History VI.13, tr. McGiffert (npnf201_eusebius-church-history-life-of-constantine l.34261-34266)

claims.claim: Card: the Refutation's Book 6 copies Irenaeus at length ('From this to the end of book vi. occurs in Irenaeus likewise')
claims.witness: Note in the American edition of the Refutation (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.10059-10064)

claims.claim: Card: Valentinus claimed to have seen a newborn child who said he was the Logos
claims.witness: Refutation VI, tr. MacMahon (anf05_hippolytus-cyprian-caius-novatian l.10053-10057). One hostile witness

claims.claim: Card: 'the disciple of Platonism'
claims.witness: Tertullian, Prescription 30, tr. Holmes (anf03_tertullian l.21332-21333)

claims.claim: Card: Axionicus at Antioch alone still kept his rules; Secundus, Marcus, Theotimus
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against the Valentinians 4 (anf03_tertullian l.43121-43127)

claims.claim: Card: 'a very large body of heretics'; earlier writers who answered them: Justin, Miltiades, Irenaeus, Proculus
claims.witness: Tertullian, Against the Valentinians 1 and 5 (anf03_tertullian l.42911-42912, 43153-43173)

claims.claim: Card: taught by Theudas, a pupil of Paul
claims.witness: Clement, Stromata VII.17, reporting the followers' claim (anf02 l.52962-52963)

contested_claims.sides: Irenaeus: from Hyginus to Anicetus (anf01_apostolic-fathers-justin-irenaeus l.39968-39970). Tertullian: in the church of Rome under Bishop Eleutherus, 'more than once expelled' (anf03_tertullian l.21332-21339).

absent_details.note: No held source read says where he was born. Epiphanius, Panarion 31 (epiphanius_ancoratus-panarion-haer-1-33-gcs-bd1-grc_holl1915.txt) was not read for this profile.
Only fragments quoted by opponents are held (Clement; the Refutation); no work of his survives whole in the held files.
